hello.note: Goedendag (KHOO-den-dakh) is the polite daytime greeting

please.note: Alsjeblieft (AHL-shuh-bleeft) is the casual form. Both also mean here you are

thank-you.note: Dank u wel (vel) means thank you very much. Bedankt (buh-DAHNKT) is the casual version

excuse-me.note: Excuseer (ek-skew-ZAIR) also works, and gets a waiter's attention

my-name.note: Ik heet... (ik hayt) also works. The audio uses Peter as the example name

speak-english.note: Most Dutch people speak excellent English

how-much.note: Wat kost dit? (vaht kost dit) means what does this cost

would-like.note: Graag makes it polite. The audio uses een koffie as the example

i-want.note: Blunt on its own; add graag to be polite. The audio uses dit (this) as the example

do-you-have.note: Put the item in the gap. The audio uses water as the example

discount.note: Haggling is unusual in shops; markets may allow a little

card.text: Kan ik met de kaart betalen?
card.say: kahn ik met duh KAHRT buh-TAH-len
card.note: Many places take only a debit card, so ask Kan ik pinnen? (PIN-nen)

taxi.text: Kunt u een taxi voor mij bellen?
taxi.say: kunt ew un TAK-see vohr my BEL-en

train-station.note: Station alone also works, and the main one is centraal station (sen-TRAHL)

which-train.note: Swap in any city; the audio uses Hanoi as the example

buy-ticket.text: Waar kan ik een kaartje kopen?
buy-ticket.say: vahr kahn ik un KAHR-tyuh KOH-pen

two-tickets.text: Kan ik twee kaartjes naar... kopen?
two-tickets.say: kahn ik tvay KAHR-tyuhs nahr ... KOH-pen
two-tickets.note: The audio uses Hanoi as the example city
two-tickets.spoken: Kan ik twee kaartjes naar Hanoi kopen?

trip-length.text: Hoe lang duurt de reis naar...?
trip-length.say: hoo LAHNG dewrt duh RYSS nahr ...
trip-length.note: The audio uses Hanoi as the example city
trip-length.spoken: Hoe lang duurt de reis naar Hanoi?

delicious.note: Lekker (LEK-er) is the everyday word for tasty

allergic.note: Add the food: noten (nuts), eieren (eggs), schaaldieren (shellfish). The audio uses noten as the example

love-dish.text: Ik ben dol op dit gerecht!
love-dish.say: ik ben DOL op dit khuh-REKHT
love-dish.note: Dol op means very fond of

what-called.note: Point at the dish or item

table-for-two.text: Een tafel voor twee personen, alstublieft
table-for-two.say: un TAH-fel vohr tvay per-SOH-nen ahl-stew-BLEEFT
table-for-two.note: For more people use drie (3) or vier (4) instead of twee

beer.note: Een pils (pils) is a small draught lager, the standard order

coffee.note: Koffie verkeerd (fer-KAYRT) is coffee with a lot of hot milk

water.note: Kraanwater (KRAHN-vah-ter) is tap water, and is safe to drink

help.note: Shout it. The police are de politie (duh poh-LEE-tsee)
